verification.reason: The code does what the cited decision says, so no documented decision is contradicted. The base decision (request-keys-as-built) says a check run's key holds "The configuration less its display keys" and names the exclusions as `output` and `publish.emoji`. `decisive` in check-request.ts strips exactly those two. The new `evidence.budget` sits in the configuration, so keying it is what the text says to do. No cited sentence forbids it, and none requires leaving a disk-limit key out. The decision's reason for the exclusions (display keys "change how a review reads and never what a check finds") does not make an exclusion list for every key like it. The same decision keys the rest of the configuration, such as `triage`, `models` and `publish`, whether or not it affects a finding. The claim describes a design gap: a new config key that causes needless check reruns when raised. It is not a departure from base text. The decision's own rule for an input on neither list is "goes to the coordinator before any fix", and that is not a requirement the head violates. The rerun behaviour in steps 4 to 7 is probably real, but it is not a contradiction of a documented decision.

verification.reason: AGENTS.md:26 says to link every GitHub issue and pull request mentioned in docs. Item 7 of the decision, at line 25, says "until issue #627 lands" with no link. Line 22 names #627 with a URL, and lines 24, 31, 33 and 37 link it. The finding cites line 24, but that line is linked. The bare mention is on line 25, so the finding's own scenario points at the right place. The file is new in this change, so base has no such text.

The doctor check uses `held < store.budget` to separate ok from warn. EvidenceStore refuses a write when `held + adding > this.budget` (packages/pipeline/src/evidence.ts:228). So a directory holding exactly the budget has no room for any non-empty write, and `<` is the correct boundary. The only doctor test (compare-evidence.test.ts:214-230) covers two cases. One is 0 B against 1 GiB. The other is a directory far past a 1 KiB budget, matched with `[0-9.]+ KiB`. Neither case sits at held == budget, so changing `<` to `<=` would pass every test. That leaves the boundary behaviour untested. I could not run the suite to confirm this.

The code does what the claim says. `EvidenceStore.write` can throw raw fs errors. `place` and `directoryFor` rethrow ENOSPC and EACCES, and `existing` and `bytes` rethrow any non-ENOENT lstat error. `keep` catches only `EvidenceError` and rethrows everything else. The adjudication was already recorded and "Adjudicated …" was already printed in compare.ts. The top-level handler in main.ts then prints `melian: <raw errno message>` and returns 1. The user gets no "the adjudication is recorded, but no evidence was kept" note. The documented behaviour in decision item 6 is written for the budget refusal. The exit code is still 1, and the "Adjudicated" line is already on stdout. So the harm is a misleading, context-free error message, not a wrong exit code or lost data.
